PullRequest.Title: Continue sessions with last applied sandbox config after managed policy conflicts
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
When a sandbox configuration update conflicts with managed policy, log the error details and continue the session with the runtime's last applied sandbox configuration instead of failing the session.

Follow-up to #338172.

## Problem
VS Code applies sandbox configuration after SDK session creation/resume and during running-session configuration updates. Previously, `applySandboxConfig` logged update errors and rethrew them, including `managed_sandbox_policy_conflict`. A rejected update could therefore fail session initialization or interrupt a request even though the runtime retained its existing sandbox configuration.

## Changes
- Catch `managed_sandbox_policy_conflict` specifically within the sandbox configuration update helper. Recognize the structured error code and the runtime's full policy-conflict message, including RPC-wrapped messages.
- Log the session context and original error details, then return without propagating that conflict.
- Continue using the runtime's existing, last applied sandbox configuration; do not retry with weaker restrictions or apply the rejected candidate.
- Return whether the update was applied, so callers preserve the last confirmed sandbox state and existing session-bypass bookkeeping when it was rejected.
- Keep existing error behavior for unrelated failures and other SDK operations.
- Document this behavior in the Agent Host guide.

## Scope
This only suppresses managed-policy conflicts from `session.options.update({ sandboxConfig })`. It does not suppress SDK resume failures, transport errors, generic unsuccessful update responses, or conflicts from other SDK operations. It does not rewrite client settings or compose managed/local filesystem policies.

## Validation
- **136 targeted tests passed** across the sandbox launcher and session permission-handling suites.
- Regression coverage includes create/resume, structured and message-based conflicts, idle and active sessions, continuing requests, preserving confirmed state, successful subsequent retries, and unrelated errors remaining failures.
- Changed-file ESLint, editor diagnostics, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Commit hygiene checks passed.

```powershell
.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotAgentSession.test.ts --grep "CopilotSessionLauncher sandbox policy|CopilotAgentSession permission handling" --reporter dot
```

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or resume a Copilot session when the sandbox update conflicts with managed policy
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SDK create/resume, script-safety options update, sandbox options update, and optional connector reconciliation must finish before the session wrapper is returned. The diff changes only the sandbox-update error outcome: a recognized conflict no longer enters disconnect-and-fail cleanup, so later initialization remains on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One create or resume attempt per ordinary launch, aside from unchanged documented resume fallbacks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SDK launch boundary ran before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Produces the raw runtime session before sandbox application can run.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical boundary ran and a conflict propagated, triggering disconnect and launch failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the wrapper is returned. The call existed before; only a recognized conflict is now converted to false.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Connector capabilities/auth/account/reconcile RPCs when connector MCP is enabled
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one fixed reconciliation sequence per launch, independent of repository size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A conflicted launch stopped before connector reconciliation, while every successful launch already performed it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These calls become reachable after a sandbox conflict because the session now continues; they were already on every successful launch path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: raw session disconnect on failed finalization
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously one after each propagated sandbox conflict; now none for recognized conflicts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A conflict entered cleanup and disconnected the raw session before surfacing failure.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One launch per session. Sandbox application is one RPC per launch; connector reconciliation is a fixed sequence per launch rather than per workspace item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Launch steps are awaited serially within a session. Separate session launches may run independently; this diff adds no burst or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The computed candidate is not cached, while the last confirmed sandbox state is intentionally retained. There is no negative conflict cache, but launch invokes this helper only once.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed catch and boolean result directly establish the new continuation path and unchanged RPC count.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime RPC latency and frequency of enterprise policy conflicts are not measured, but launch cardinality is fixed and small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Continuing through later initialization adds work only because the launch now succeeds; it neither multiplies the sandbox boundary nor introduces unbounded retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Apply a live sandbox configuration change while the session is idle or has an active turn
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The configuration event queues permission synchronization when needed and one sandbox options.update. A recognized conflict now resolves normally, preserves confirmed state, and avoids the prior error/rollback/active-turn abort path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: permissions.setMode and experimental options update when active permission settings require changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one of each changed permission setting per relevant event, with state checks avoiding unchanged mode writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes sandbox application for active turns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per matching sandbox/approval configuration event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same RPC propagated conflicts to the outer handler.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by the per-session sequencer; the changed helper turns only managed conflicts into a normal false result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Session abort after active-turn synchronization failure
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously one after a managed conflict during an active turn; now zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The outer catch aborted an active turn after the conflict propagated.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One sandbox RPC per relevant configuration event. Event handling is scoped to the owning session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Sandbox updates are serialized by _sandboxConfigSequencer per session; active sessions remain independent. No new parallel fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The last confirmed state is retained because false suppresses publication of the rejected candidate. The rejected candidate is not negatively cached, allowing a later event or turn to retry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the event filter, sequencers, and tests demonstrate exactly one immediate rejected update and removal of abort behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Configuration-event frequency is user/policy driven, but each event has bounded cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The diff removes failure cleanup and preserves state without adding per-item work, concurrency, or retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send or resume turns after a managed-policy conflict remains active
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every normal send/resume runs _prepareSdkTurn serially before the provider call. Its sandbox step retries one options.update; the new false result allows shell/MCP reconciliation and the actual send to proceed instead of failing the turn.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per send/resume/fleet turn; tests explicitly show a second attempt on the first turn after an event conflict.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Successful sessions already issued one sandbox update per turn; a managed conflict instead rejected the turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the provider send. The boundary and per-turn frequency predate the diff; the conflict branch now continues afterward.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Materialize a configured shell init script
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One write when configured script content is synchronized; not per sandbox conflict once registered.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing shell synchronization ran on successful preparation; a propagated sandbox conflict prevented reaching it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: May be awaited after the sandbox step during turn preparation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: MCP list and per-server enable/disable reconciliation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One list only when desired MCP enablement is nonempty, then at most one operation per server whose observed state differs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing on successful turns; a propagated sandbox conflict prevented reaching it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited after sandbox and shell synchronization before the provider send.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider request per accepted turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A conflict blocked this request; successful turns already used it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The user-visible agent turn starts after preparation; the diff makes this reachable after recognized conflicts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Warning log including the conflict Error object
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One warning per rejected attempt, therefore one per turn while conflict persists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The generic failure path also logged the same error once, but the failed session could not accumulate later per-turn warnings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous log invocation occurs in the rejected RPC path; downstream sink behavior is not established as blocking.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One sandbox RPC and warning per turn while the same conflict persists; typical multiplicity follows conversation turn count, not files, tools, or repository size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-session sandbox, shell, and MCP work is sequenced; preparation steps are awaited serially. Different sessions can prepare independently, as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no negative cache for a rejected sandbox candidate, so a persistent conflict is retried on each turn. Successful sandbox configs were already re-applied on every turn before this diff, and retry preserves the ability to recover when runtime policy changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that one retry and warning occur per turn; low that this bounded work constitutes a material regression rather than the necessary cost of newly continued functionality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The actual cost of a local SDK RPC and log sink is unknown. A persistent conflict can repeat across turns, but the fixed one-call cardinality matches the pre-existing successful-turn contract and no evidence shows material latency or log-volume impact.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Although the conflict is not negatively cached, the retry is a single serialized RPC per turn, successful sessions already paid the same per-turn RPC, and retry is required to recover from runtime-side policy changes without a proven invalidation signal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Register or refresh a shell init script while sandbox application conflicts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Script materialization writes the file, then sandbox application is awaited before registering the path. A recognized conflict now allows the existing shell registration RPC to proceed while retaining runtime policy.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One write per changed script synchronization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unchanged and already occurred before a propagated sandbox conflict.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs before sandbox validation and registration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Sandbox options update followed by shell initScripts options update
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sandbox update and, for a new path, one shell registration RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The shell registration was reached after successful sandbox application but not after a propagated conflict.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both are awaited during synchronization; the shell registration becomes reachable after a recognized conflict.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One filesystem write per script content synchronization and one registration RPC per new path; content changes rewrite in place without another registration.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Shell synchronization is serialized by _shellInitScriptSequencer, and sandbox application is independently serialized by _sandboxConfigSequencer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Serialized script content and registered path suppress repeated registration. A conflict does not alter these caches; the runtime's existing sandbox state remains authoritative.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: path caching and sequencer ownership are explicit in the implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Shell init scripts are optional and registration frequency is path-bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The newly reachable registration is bounded and represents completion of requested initialization, not repeated or fan-out work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and traced launch, live configuration, per-turn preparation, and shell synchronization. The PR changes recognized managed-policy conflicts from fatal to non-fatal while retaining existing serialized RPC cardinality. No high-confidence actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
